summary: OGC GeoPose is a small, finished standard that does one job: say where something is on Earth and which way it is facing, in a form two systems can exchange. The document records an approval date of 2022-06-20 and a publication date of 2023-09-08, so calling it a draft seeking uplift, as our own older research did, is wrong. It is a data structure and not a service: the word resolve does not appear anywhere in it, and it states plainly that it does not constrain services or interfaces, so it never turns a name into a place you can reach. Its two simple forms pin the outer frame to the world geodetic system of 1984, while the flexible form only names an outside frame authority and says reading that name is somebody else's job, so two systems can exchange a valid pose and still disagree about where it is. One trap for anyone citing it: the published rule for latitude reads that the minimum value shall be 90.0 degrees and the maximum value shall be 90.0 degrees, with the minus sign missing, while the neighbouring rule for longitude correctly carries its minus sign.

coverage.note: The whole point of the standard: one agreed way to hand the position and orientation of a real or virtual object from one system to another, in a frame tied to the Earth or to another astronomical body.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: The two simple forms fix the frame: an implicit world geodetic system of 1984 datum with a local tangent plane. The flexible form instead carries three strings naming an outside authority, an identifier and parameters, and the standard says reading them is not its job. So the frame is named but never defined, and two conforming systems can exchange a pose whose frame they interpret differently.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: The interpretation of the contents of these fields is outside the scope of GeoPose.

coverage.note: Axis order and rotation order are pinned down: East, North and Up map to X, Y and Z; yaw, pitch and roll are three rotations about the local z, y and x axes applied in that order; quaternion parts are written w, x, y, z. What is missing is scale and any general transform composition, because version 1.0 allows only movement and turning, and the word handed appears nowhere in the document.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: This abstraction is constrained in GeoPose v1.0 to only allow transformations involving translation and rotation.

coverage.note: Units are fixed for the pose itself: height in metres above the reference ellipsoid, latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. Nothing is said about the size of whatever content is placed at that pose, so it does not settle whether an imported model arrives at the right scale.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: SHALL be expressed as a height in meters above the WGS-84 ellipsoid

coverage.note: Time series and stream forms carry a time stamp per pose, but the time model is deliberately thin: whole and fractional seconds of one common clock count, with no clock agreement, no ordering rules and no drift handling. It timestamps poses; it does not give two machines a shared clock.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: GeoPose v1.0 has a very restricted idea of time position, limited to seconds of UNIX Time.

coverage.note: It carries a normative abstract test suite as Annex A, eight independent conformance classes with no dependency between them, and published schemas that encoded objects must validate against. This is one of the few subjects on this map that ships a test suite with the specification.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: Conformance with this standard shall be checked using all the relevant tests specified in Annex A of this document.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard, Annex A Abstract Test Suite
sources.quote: A.4.4 Advanced SDU Conformance Class; A.4.2 through A.4.9 define eight SDU conformance classes; A.3 defines three common classes; A.2 defines a global class; A.5 defines eight JSON encoding classes

coverage.note: It supplies the shared vocabulary two devices need to state where a thing is, and nothing else. There is no anchor identifier, no way to store or fetch an anchor, no persistence rule and no service, and the standard says outright that it does not constrain services or interfaces. Treat it as the payload for a shared anchor, not as shared anchoring.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: the Standard does not assume or constrain services or interfaces providing conversion between GeoPoses of difference types or relying on different external reference frame definitions.

coverage.note: A pose is not an address. A full text read of the standard finds no occurrence of the word resolve, and no resolution mechanism of any kind. Anyone hoping this fills the place-naming hole should look elsewhere.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: the Standard does not assume or constrain services or interfaces providing conversion between GeoPoses of difference types or relying on different external reference frame definitions.

coverage.note: Recovering a pose from camera pictures appears only in the use case table, as work that produces a GeoPose. The standard specifies no method, no imagery handling and no matching. It is the output container for a visual positioning system, not the system.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: Instantaneous and time series location and orientation of an optical imaging device using Simultaneous Location And Mapping (SLAM)

coverage.note: It carries a pose, not the content placed at it. There is no tiling, no geometry payload and no streaming of terrain or city data. That boundary is worth stating explicitly, because the other geospatial subject on this map does exactly that job.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: The Frame Transform is the core abstraction in the GeoPose Standard.

coverage.note: It can carry where a camera is and which way it points, which is a listed use case, and that is the whole contribution. It defines no field of view, no projection, no viewpoint binding and no rule for moving between viewpoints.

coverage.note: GeoPose is exactly the transform half of this row and none of the rest. A pose is a frame transform relating an outer frame to an inner one, which is the very thing two maps of one place need between them, and the standard even packages sequenced and linked transforms. What it never does is declare that a map exists, give it a version and a lifecycle, or name the two maps a transform is between.

coverage.note: The standard allows extra JSON members and itself calls application-specific needs outside its scope, so declared descriptive metadata for a scene is not its purpose; the permissive-encoding tolerance is scored under deliver.extension.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 9.2.1 JSON encoding
sources.quote: In addition to supporting specific application requirements outside the GeoPose 1.0 scope

coverage.note: Searched GeoPose 1.0 (21-056r11, full text with its embedded JSON schemas, Clauses 1 to 10 and Annexes A to E) for privacy, anonym, pseudonym, retention, consent, coarse, obfusc, confidential and personal on 2026-10-20; no match, and the Security considerations section says none were made. A pose can locate a real device or person, so the gap is real.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Security considerations
sources.quote: No security considerations have been made for this document.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 1 Scope
sources.quote: interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: The Graph and Chain targets carry a directed acyclic graph of linked frame transforms between poses; what is missing is any object content, names or properties on the nodes, so it is a pose graph rather than a scene graph.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 8.4.4 Requirements class 8: Graph
sources.quote: The Graph Target supports a network of object relative poses.

coverage.note: The Chain target carries a linear sequence of frame transformations for modelling articulated structures, and the Graph target carries a network of relative poses, so together they hold the hierarchy half of a rig; missing are standard bone names, skin binding, weights and joint limits.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), A.5.6 Chain SDU JSON conformance class
sources.quote: The GeoPose Chain JSON encoding supports a linear sequence of frame transformations for modelling articulated structures.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 6.4.4 Table 5, use case se/01
sources.quote: Record pose relationships of all mobile elements in an environment

coverage.note: The series and stream targets store time-stamped poses and a transition model that says how to estimate poses between them, but the transition model is only a named authority with parameters, and there are no clips or properties other than pose.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 6.4.4 Table 5, use case se/02
sources.quote: Control animation of mobile elements in an environment using stored pose time sequences

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 4.3.8 transition model
sources.quote: metadata that indicates whether or how it may be possible to estimate poses

coverage.note: The Stream target defines the form of an open-ended series of time-stamped poses, which covers the form of pose state; which state is shared, how often it is sent and how it is delivered are not specified.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 2.3 Standardization targets
sources.quote: Open-ended sequence of time-stamped GeoPoses: Stream Target

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 8.4.8 Stream
sources.quote: In the delivery of a stream the Header and Elements are not part of a single data structure that exists at a single instant.

coverage.note: The permissive JSON encodings allow added properties so a later version can extend objects without breaking validation of old ones, but no object carries a version member and the standard states no compatibility rule.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 9.2.1 JSON encoding
sources.quote: this flexibility enables experimentation with useful properties that might be part of a future version of the OGC GeoPose Standard.

coverage.note: GeoPose specifies how to exchange the position and orientation of an object on or near the Earth. It has no payment exchange.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose only states where an object is and which way it faces; holders and grants are not part of it.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0, Abstract
sources.quote: The OGC GeoPose 1.0 Standard defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose exchanges the location and orientation of objects, so a record of purchase or grant is not something it expresses.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: GeoPose 1.0 is an OGC Implementation Standard for exchanging the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects

coverage.note: GeoPose exchanges the position and orientation of objects and does not govern which issuers or worlds are accepted, so a governed trust registry is outside it.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: GeoPose 1.0 is an OGC Implementation Standard for exchanging the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects

coverage.note: GeoPose defines the exchange of location and orientation of objects, which is a pose format and not a stream of body signals such as heart rate or skin conductance.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 1 Scope
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose is a data structure for exchanging location and orientation, so it has no authoring or publishing interface for an outside agent.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose standardises how the location and orientation of an object is written down and exchanged; it defines a Stream target of time-stamped poses (recorded under geo.trajectory), but no binding or transport that connects a world object to a live sensor or controller.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose standardizes the location and orientation of objects; it states where something is, not what a person did or with what result.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose defines how to state where something is and which way it faces, not how to export a place, so whole-place export is outside it.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard (21-056r11, version 1.0.0), Clause 1 Scope
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose defines how to exchange the location and orientation of objects; it is a data structure and does not render or stream frames.

sources.title: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Data Exchange Standard
sources.quote: defines requirements (rules) for the interoperable exchange of the location and orientation of real or virtual geometric objects (poses)

coverage.note: GeoPose is the data structure for stating where something is and which way it faces once something has measured it; it defines no recognition, though a tracker's output could be carried in it.
